"Welcome aboard the evening ferry, please keep your bags clear of the doors."

Deliver it as spoken audio in `./announcement.wav`, a WAV file of 4 to 8 seconds that a passenger can understand.

**Goal:** deliver `./announcement.wav` — the spoken ferry announcement, 4–8 s, understandable.

**Action:** generated it with the Windows built-in TTS (`System.Speech`, default voice, normal rate) via a PowerShell script, writing with `SetOutputToWaveStream` (the `SaveToWave` method is missing on this .NET runtime, so the first script failed and I switched approach).

diff:
A tts.ps1
A verify.ps1

--- tts.ps1 ---
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Speech
$path = "$PSScriptRoot\announcement.wav"
$fs = [System.IO.File]::OpenWrite($path)
$s = New-Object System.Speech.Synthesis.SpeechSynthesizer
$s.SetOutputToWaveStream($fs)
$s.Speak("Welcome aboard the evening ferry, please keep your bags clear of the doors.")
$s.Dispose()
$fs.Flush()
$fs.Dispose()
$f = Get-Item $path
Write-Output ("Bytes: " + $f.Length)


--- verify.ps1 ---
$p = "$PSScriptRoot\announcement.wav"
$b = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($p)
$rate = [BitConverter]::ToInt32($b, 24)
$bits = [BitConverter]::ToInt16($b, 22)
$ch = [BitConverter]::ToInt16($b, 20)
$bytes = $b.Length - 44
$dur = $bytes / ($rate * [int]($bits / 8) * $ch)
Write-Output ("Rate: " + $rate)
Write-Output ("Channels: " + $ch)
Write-Output ("Bits: " + $bits)
Write-Output ("Duration: " + $dur.ToString("F2") + "s")
$max = 0
for ($i = 44; $i -lt $b.Length - 1; $i += 2) {
  $v = [Math]::Abs([BitConverter]::ToInt16($b, $i))
  if ($v -gt $max) { $max = $v }
}
Write-Output ("MaxSample: " + $max)
